title: Runtime kernel continuity shim for mixed FlashAttention v2/v3 workloads with stochastic prefill patterns
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: After integrating FlashAttention v3 kernels we observe intermittent latency regressions and decode jitter for mixed-model traffic where some requests use v2-compatible variants and others are routed to v3. Root causes appear correlated with rapid kernel hotswaps during bursty prefill sequences and head-splitting differences between v2/v3 kernel layouts. This ticket scopes a lightweight runtime shim that enforces kernel continuity for a request's prefill->decode phase and provides a probing mode to gather targeted telemetry before a staged rollout. Goal: eliminate p95 decode latency spikes for mixed workloads without regressing steady-state throughput across common sequence length distributions.
acceptance_criteria: Canary demonstrates <5% increase in p50 decode latency and no >5% increase in p95 for 95% of traffic shapes
No increase in OOM or memory safety errors during canary compared to baseline
Telemetry surfaces per-request kernel decision events and durations for prefill and decode phases
Rollback switch available that returns behavior to pre-v3 kernel routing in <1 minute
steps: 1) Implement continuity shim that pins kernel class for a request from prefill through decode (code change + config toggle)
2) Add lightweight per-request kernel_decision telemetry (kernel_id, chosen_variant, reason, time_ms prefill/decode)
3) Create a probing mode: 1% of requests sample alternate kernel (v2 vs v3) in parallel and record diff metrics
4) Run offline microbenchmarks across representative shapes (seq=64/128/512/2048), precision combos (fp16/int8), and batch sizes
5) Execute staged canary on dedicated pool with traffic mirroring and ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%, with rollback gates
6) Post-canary: bake telemetry into console dashboards and add alerting for kernel oscillation/latency delta
comments: 2026-02-20 - Ava Martinez: Created ticket after triage. Observed regression cluster in canaries spanning 2026-02-16. Initial hypothesis: kernel hot-swap during prefill/first decode tokens causes cache thrashing and path divergence for v3 tiled layouts.

2026-02-23 - Rohit Sharma: Ran unit microbenchmarks comparing v2/v3 on A100 80GB. Found 8-12% higher p95 for mixed routing when sequence splits cross 512 boundary. Suspect workspace reuse and allocator fragmentation.

2026-02-26 - Priya Nair (perf): Prototype shim committed on feature-branch. Shim pins kernel class at request start and prevents switching unless kernel is incompatible (explicit fallback). Added local telemetry hooks.

2026-03-02 - QA: Integration tests flagged a regression for very short multiplexed prefill (seq<32) where shim increased per-request latency by ~3%. Plan: narrow scope to pin continuity only when prefill length > 64 or when model declares nontrivial head-splitting.

2026-03-05 - Rohit Sharma: Updated probing mode to sample 0.5% by default; increased to 1% for internal QA pool. Added experiment to collect delta of decode token latency per-request between primary and sampled kernel.

2026-03-09 - Observability: Dashboard panels added for kernel_oscillation_rate, per-kernel p50/p95 decode latency, and prefill->decode transition time. Created alert 'kernel-switch-latency-delta' threshold=15ms p95.

2026-03-10 - Rohit Sharma: Running canary (1% traffic) for internal dev cluster; preliminary results: p95 decode latency reduced by 18% for mixed workloads vs baseline, steady-state throughput unchanged. Next step: broaden shapes and run 5% canary.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Shim may introduce small tail latency increases for very short prefill sequences. Mitigation: conditional enablement (prefill_len >= 64) and per-model override in model manifest.

Risk: Incorrect pinning could block legitimate fallback from v3->v2 leading to correctness or OOM. Mitigation: allow shim to detect incompatibility and trigger safe fallback path; add safety unit tests and canary OOM monitoring.
Risk: Telemetry volume increase. Mitigation: telemetry sampling for high-traffic customers and aggregation at route-level; default low sampling rate for production.
